description: The APPROXIMATE numerics carry no precision and no scale. The engine keeps a nominal (38,9) inside its FLOAT type, and the question is which surfaces that pair is allowed to reach: none of them. Live answers the same six-alias table on every surface - SHOW COLUMNS prints the family alone, {"type":"REAL","nullable":true}, with no numbers beside it; DESCRIBE spells the bare word FLOAT; INFORMATION_SCHEMA leaves data_type FLOAT with numeric_precision and numeric_scale both NULL, which is how it says no pair; and GET_DDL writes every alias back as an unparameterised FLOAT. A NUMBER(10,2) sitting in the same table does carry its pair on all four, so the absence is the family's own rule rather than a missing feature. FLOAT, DOUBLE, REAL, FLOAT4, FLOAT8 and DOUBLE PRECISION are ONE type with six spellings, so all six answer identically. Converted from types/ApproximateNumericMetadataTest, which keeps only its JDBC-driver test (see the task note); the class's helper lookups become SHOW COLUMNS and DESCRIBE TABLE read back through RESULT_SCAN, and the GET_DDL containment checks become CONTAINS over the same text.

steps.sql: CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ft (f FLOAT, d DOUBLE, r REAL, f4 FLOAT4, f8 FLOAT8, dp DOUBLE PRECISION, n NUMBER(10,2))
SELECT "column_name" || ' => ' || "data_type" AS r FROM TABLE(RESULT_SCAN(LAST_QUERY_ID())) ORDER BY r
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ft (f FLOAT, d DOUBLE, r REAL, f4 FLOAT4, f8 FLOAT8, dp DOUBLE PRECISION, n NUMBER(10,2))
SELECT "name" || ' => ' || "type" AS r FROM TABLE(RESULT_SCAN(LAST_QUERY_ID())) ORDER BY r
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ft (f FLOAT, d DOUBLE, r REAL, f4 FLOAT4, f8 FLOAT8, dp DOUBLE PRECISION, n NUMBER(10,2))

SELECT column_name || ' => ' || data_type || '/' || COALESCE(TO_VARCHAR(numeric_precision), 'NULL') || '/' || COALESCE(TO_VARCHAR(numeric_scale), 'NULL') AS r FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name = 'FT' ORDER BY ordinal_position
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ft (f FLOAT, d DOUBLE, r REAL, f4 FLOAT4, f8 FLOAT8, dp DOUBLE PRECISION, n NUMBER(10,2))

SELECT TO_VARCHAR(CONTAINS(g, 'F FLOAT,') AND CONTAINS(g, 'D FLOAT,') AND CONTAINS(g, 'R FLOAT,') AND CONTAINS(g, 'F4 FLOAT,') AND CONTAINS(g, 'F8 FLOAT,') AND CONTAINS(g, 'DP FLOAT,')) AS r FROM (SELECT GET_DDL('TABLE', 'ft') AS g)
SELECT TO_VARCHAR(CONTAINS(g, 'N NUMBER(10,2)')) AS r FROM (SELECT GET_DDL('TABLE', 'ft') AS g)
SELECT TO_VARCHAR(CONTAINS(g, 'FLOAT(')) AS r FROM (SELECT GET_DDL('TABLE', 'ft') AS g)
